name: El Cajon
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in El Cajon, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in El Cajon, CA: Winter Wonderland at Wells Park with train rides, downtown Holiday Lights, Jingle Bell Hill and more.
lede: El Cajon does Christmas downtown and in its parks: a tree lighting and holiday lights on Main Street, a free Winter Wonderland morning at Wells Park, and a whole hillside of neighborhood lights.
celebrates: The Downtown El Cajon Association opens the season with Holiday Lights in Downtown El Cajon, an evening of live music, holiday shopping and the official tree lighting at Prescott Promenade on East Main Street. In December, City of El Cajon Parks and Recreation hosts Winter Wonderland at Wells Park, a free morning of train rides, bounce houses, a movie in the park, character photos and crafts with the El Cajon Rec Squad, and this year a Breakfast with Santa. Neighbors around Pepper Drive and Lindenwood Drive light up Jingle Bell Hill from the day after Thanksgiving to New Year's Day, and The Magnolia stages holiday shows such as The Nutcracker.
lastyear: In 2025 the Downtown El Cajon Association held Holiday Lights in Downtown El Cajon on Saturday, November 29, from 4 to 8 pm. Its invitation promised a night of festive fun, live music, holiday shopping and the official tree lighting ceremony at 6:15 pm, and asked families to come make memories under the lights. The association later posted its photo albums from the evening and from its 2025 Pictures with Santa sessions.
facts: El Cajon means the box in Spanish. The city takes its name from the Big Box Valley, a valley ringed by foothills on every side. The old land grant called Rancho Cajon once covered the present communities of Lakeside, Santee, Bostonia, El Cajon and part of Grossmont. On November 12, 1912, 123 of 158 voters chose to incorporate a small area around Main Street and Magnolia Avenue, and by 1940 the city still had only 1,471 residents.
trains: El Cajon is a trolley town. The MTS Green and Orange Lines both run to the El Cajon Transit Center, and from there the Copper Line continues to Santee, the route MTS recommends for reaching Santee's holiday lighting. Kids can also ride a trackless train at Winter Wonderland in Wells Park. For a real Christmas train, the Pacific Southwest Railway Museum in Campo runs its North Pole Limited farther east in the county, and the San Diego Model Railroad Museum fills a hall in Balboa Park with layouts.

kidfact: El Cajon means the box in Spanish. The town got that name because hills surround its valley on every side, like the walls of a box.
faq: Where is the El Cajon Christmas tree lighting?

The official tree lighting is part of Holiday Lights in Downtown El Cajon, hosted by the Downtown El Cajon Association at Prescott Promenade on East Main Street. In 2025 the event ran from 4 to 8 pm on November 29 with live music and holiday shopping, and the tree was lit at 6:15 pm.
Is Winter Wonderland in El Cajon free?

Yes. City of El Cajon Parks and Recreation lists every Winter Wonderland activity at Wells Park as free, including train rides, bounce houses, a movie in the park, photos with costumed characters and arts and crafts. Breakfast with Santa is also free but needs preregistration, and the city keeps a waitlist when seatings fill.
What is Jingle Bell Hill in El Cajon?

Jingle Bell Hill is a neighborhood Christmas light display in El Cajon around Pepper Drive and Lindenwood Drive. The neighbors keep the homes lit in the evenings, from 5 to 10 pm, starting the day after Thanksgiving and running through New Year's Day. The display has its own website, jinglebellhill.com, with photos and updates.
Can we take the trolley to El Cajon for Christmas events?

Yes. The MTS Green and Orange Lines both stop at the El Cajon Transit Center, and the Copper Line runs on from there to Santee. For Santee's holiday lighting, MTS strongly recommended taking transit because parking near the event is limited, and its riders can park for free at transit station lots.
